correctness.rationale: For every n>=2, slice membership at height t is given by nonnegativity and sum_i(x_i-(1-t))_+<=t. Maximizing subset sums gives the complete halfspaces. At interior heights the coordinate faces have dimension n-1 and each size-k subset face is the product of the translated t-scaled coordinate (k-1)-simplex with the (1-t)-scaled (n-k)-cube; varying height gives facets, and both end layers are n-dimensional. Eliminating one x_i in a subset facet gives the induced Gram matrix I+uu^T with squared norm of u equal to (k-1)+(k-1)^2, hence metric factor sqrt(k^2-k+1). In the remaining n coordinates the volume integrates t^(k-1)(1-t)^(n-k)/(k-1)!, giving the exact area. Partition by excess coordinates and integrate the beta factors to verify V_n and the coordinate-facet areas. Summation verifies the increment and the first omitted increment dominates the residual factorial tail. The rank tail, fixed-K area concentration and binomial count-rank comparison then follow as stated. The independent Gram and numerical-series checks use record4() in /workspace/branches/frozen_metric_replay.py; they do not replace the analytic proof. The frozen hull diagnostic was read, not run.

evidence: For each j, the earlier slice product has area sqrt(j)t^(j-1)(1-t)^(n-j)/(j-1)!, using the elementary coordinate simplex area. The earlier facet equation fixes the coarea multiplier sqrt((j^2-j+1)/j). Integrating gives sqrt(j^2-j+1)(n-j)!/n! exactly.

Multiplying by binomial(n,j) leaves sqrt(j^2-j+1)/j!. The entire rank law and its dimension-independent factorial tail then follow by dividing by the sum including the end-layer and coordinate contributions.

Nonnegativity makes this a coordinate face; both second-block layer factors contain 0, so the induced Euclidean body in (x,t) is exactly C_k.

The cube and simplex are also the order polytope of an antichain and stable-set polytope of a complete graph, respectively. Hibi–Ohsugi–Tsuchiya place the layers in the reverse order, rectified by t↦1-t.
